saints.name: St. Willibald
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: An English monk whose long pilgrimage to the Holy Land preceded a lifetime of missionary labor…
biography: Born in Wessex about the year 700, son of Richard the Pilgrim and a kinsman of Boniface, Willibald entered the monastery of Waldheim as a child. In 721 he set out with his father and his brother Winibald for Rome; the father died on the way at Lucca, but the brothers pressed on through Italy.

In 724 Willibald sailed from Naples for the East — Ephesus, Cyprus, Antioch, and the Holy Land, reaching Jerusalem in November 725 — then spent two years at Constantinople before returning to a decade as a monk of Monte Cassino. He was the first Englishman known to have visited the Holy Land, and in old age dictated his itinerary, the Hodoeporicon, to the nun Huneberc of Heidenheim.

Summoned by Boniface to the German mission, he was ordained priest in 741 and about 746 was consecrated first bishop of Eichstätt, where he labored for over forty years; with Winibald he founded the double monastery of Heidenheim, later ruled by their sister Walburga. He died in 787 and was canonized in 938 by Leo VII.
saints.knownFor: His pilgrimage to the Holy Land and mission among the Germans.
